transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Devin Shaw (Redwood SE), Arjun Patel (Redwood Solutions), Marcelo Ruiz (Aurora CTO), Priya Nair (Aurora Cloud Architect), Sam Cho (Aurora Security), Elena Voss (Aurora PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Align on packaging for marketplace listing and edge reference architecture; identify security gating and perf benchmark plan.

00:00:10 Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I see we have most folks — quick intro round?
00:00:18 Marcelo: yeah marcelo here CTO, thanks. we're eager to get the listing, but also need the edge pattern nailed down, cause we run satellites and edge relays that have intermittent connectivity.
00:00:32 Devin: yeah hi all, devin from redwood, i'll drive the tech pieces — we did a quick pre-read of aurora's network topology, some questions there.
00:00:39 Priya: thanks, quick context — we have multiple sites, each with a small GPU pool; some are air-gapped, some on public cloud. need VPC-style peering in marketplace offering, and strong KMS integration.
00:00:54 Arjun: got it. our main goal is twofold: marketplace listing that customers can click-to-deploy in their private cloud, and a reference architecture for hybrid onprem/edge installs.
00:01:05 Sam: and from security — SSO, audit logs, key ownership, and E2E encryption at rest is non-negotiable.
00:01:13 Lena: good, that matches typical enterprise asks. we'll go through packaging, auth/KMS, and perf/quantization tradeoffs.

00:03:05 Devin: first, packaging. For marketplace we recommend a minimal helm chart that references a private image and an operator option for upgrades. important: the chart must expose KMS integration points (env var + mount), and allow disabling telemetry for air-gapped sites.
00:03:27 Priya: can that helm chart accept a sealed-secret or native cloud KMS provider? we can't accept plaintext keys.
00:03:36 Devin: yes, we support both. chart will accept the KMS provider type: aws-kms, gcp-kms, azure-keyvault, or bring-your-own-HSM. docs will show secret annotation examples.
00:03:49 Priya: okay good. also about the operator — do you expect we run the operator centrally or per-site?
00:03:56 Devin: recommended: per-cluster operator for lifecycle and automatic kv-cache warmers. central operator complicates network egress for air-gapped.

00:06:12 Sam: audit logs — do you ship structured logs or push to a sidecar? our SOC needs immutable logs with tenant id and request hash.
00:06:22 Arjun: we emit structured JSON audit events; for private deployments they can write to local syslog or forward to their ELK/Graylog. we'll include an audit-log adapter config in the chart.
00:06:34 Sam: any chance transcription of model calls are kept? we need retention policies.
00:06:39 Lena: retention's configurable. default is 30 days for hosted, but for Private/VPC deployments we surface retention through values in the chart so you can disable or set to 0.

00:08:50 Priya: networking — how does the marketplace listing wire up if customers require private endpoints only? we can't open public ingress for some sites.
00:08:58 Devin: two patterns: 1) marketplace listing that deploys only control-plane components to customer VPC with no public egress; 2) a hybrid gateway that uses customer-managed peering or an SSH-based connector. we'll document both.
00:09:16 Priya: the SSH connector sounds promising — but does it require persistent outbound connections?
00:09:22 Devin: yes short-lived handshake with keepalive windows; it's compatible with intermittent connectivity, we implement message queueing at the gateway for in-flight requests.

00:12:01 Marcelo: performance — our primary ask is predictable tail latency. our P50 target is 120ms and P95 under 900ms for a 1k token request at 8 QPS per site. is that realistic with quantized models?
00:12:17 Devin: depends on model variant. default approach: provide smaller quantized variant for edge (4-bit q8_0 or dynamic int8) and larger model in hosted/dedicated. quantization will drop latency and memory but may impact quality. we recommend a canary: route 5% to quantized model and monitor eval set.
00:12:36 Arjun: also caching. our runtime supports prefix and KV caching. at edge you can persist KV cache to local SSD so warm start reduces P95 significantly.
00:12:49 Marcelo: interesting, local SSD for KV cache — is that part of the helm values?
00:12:53 Devin: yes, values allow localCache.enabled=true, localCache.path=/var/lib/redwood/cache. we also provide a cache eviction policy config.

00:15:20 Priya: about model licensing and marketplace terms — does Redwood allow us to ship models that are pre-quantized, or do you need to vet each model?
00:15:29 Lena: marketplace listing will have a model catalog entry. if you're shipping pre-quantized models you must include provenance and a vetting checklist. we can include an attest file and a checksum in the chart.
00:15:42 Priya: checksum yeah that's good.

00:17:05 Sam: encryption — how do you integrate with our HSM? we use on-prem Thales with PKCS#11.
00:17:12 Devin: we already have an HSM adapter. the operator mounts PKCS#11 creds; helm values accept pkcs11.slot and pkcs11.pin secret ref. we'd need a test integration in your staging to certify.
00:17:25 Sam: ok we'll provision that.

00:20:00 Arjun: deployment patterns for intermittent connectivity: we recommend queued mode where inference requests are accepted locally, processed against the KV-warmed model, and if model variant is unavailable we fallback to a lightweight local transformer for on-device fallback, else queue for offload when connectivity resumes.
00:20:18 Marcelo: fallback to local small transformer — are you shipping that runtime?
00:20:22 Devin: yes we provide a tiny runtime binary (arm64/x86) as part of the chart, optional component. it supports reduced-context models for emergency fallback.

00:22:37 Priya: telemetry — can we opt out entirely for air-gapped?
00:22:43 Lena: yes, telemetry is optional. we'll provide a signed config to disable only telemetry that leaves cluster. internal metrics are still available for health checks.

00:25:12 Devin: let's talk canary and routing. For marketplace listing we propose a routing policy: default local deployment uses model-pin v1.2; we recommend canary route allowing 5% or 10% traffic to new variant with automatic rollback if quality/regression triggers exceed threshold.
00:25:27 Priya: what's the mechanism for regression detection?
00:25:30 Arjun: tie rollouts to eval suite and a prompt set. we can compute BLEU/ROUGE-ish heuristics for structured outputs, plus human spot checks in UAT. automatic rollback on error-rate and latency SLO breach.

00:28:10 Marcelo: compliance question — we need a paper trail for who invoked what. can your audit logs capture token counts and returned vectors?
00:28:19 Devin: we capture token level metrics and request hashes. vector outputs are not stored by default; we can configure to log vector lengths and a vector-hash if needed for debugging while preserving content privacy.

00:30:45 Sam: legal will ask about data residency — when deployed via marketplace in customer's VPC all data stays in-customer unless they opt-in to Redwood managed model updates, correct?
00:30:54 Lena: correct. auto model pulls are opt-in. we support offline update packages for air-gapped customers.

00:33:00 Priya: about marketplace listing UI — does Redwood provide a one-click deploy experience that wires KMS and privatelink or do we need to author a listing doc?
00:33:10 Lena: we provide templates; Aurora will need to populate the listing metadata, include CloudFormation/ARM/Terraform snippets for network peering and the helm chart. we also require a preflight validation script — we'll help with that.

00:36:12 Devin: benchmark plan: we suggest a 48-hour stress run on Aurora staging with two phases: 1) steady-state QPS to observe memory/latency drift, 2) burst tests to validate autoscale. collect P50/P95/P99 and token throughput, plus KV-cache hit rates.
00:36:31 Marcelo: can Redwood orchestrate the load runner or should we provide a harness?
00:36:37 Devin: Redwood can coordinate and provide a lightweight load harness; we'll want sample payloads from you.

00:39:55 Priya: quantization tradeoffs — any pointer on accuracy drop for q4 vs q8 for typical instruction-tuned models?
00:40:03 Devin: general rule: q8 tends to preserve quality for chat-like instruction-tuned models; q4 may reduce quality on long-form generation and some arithmetic. we recommend starting with q8_0 and evaluating on your prompt set.
00:40:15 Arjun: we can include an A/B eval harness in the helm values so UAT can run comparisons automatically.

00:42:30 Lena: let's surface a concrete timeline: we'll deliver refarch diagram and helm-chart skeleton by 2027-04-07, you'll provide payload samples by 2027-04-04, and we schedule perf run week of 2027-04-11. does that sound ok?
00:42:46 Marcelo: yes, works for us.

00:45:00 Sam: one more security ask — do you support tamper-evident logs and do you have an HMAC for each event?
00:45:07 Devin: yes we can sign events with HMAC using a per-tenant key stored in the HSM. that's part of the audit adapter.

00:47:20 Elena: for the marketplace listing, we'll need marketing copy and a pricing tier suggestion. who on Redwood handles that?
00:47:27 Lena: our partner marketing lead will help; we'll coordinate post-call and share a template.

00:49:55 Priya: small nit — helm values for localCache.path, is there a recommended disk IO? many of our edge nodes have eMMC.
00:50:04 Devin: recommend SSD or NVMe if available; for eMMC we provide a smaller in-memory cache and a reduced token window to avoid write amplification. we'll document config thresholds.

00:52:30 Marcelo: any blockers we foresee?
00:52:34 Arjun: main blockers: getting HSM creds into staging, and sample payloads for perf; otherwise packaging is straightforward.

00:54:10 Lena: recap — action items and owners posted in chat. we'll follow up with the diagram and playbook. Next meeting: perf-run kickoff after you deliver samples.
00:54:26 Marcelo: thanks everyone.
00:54:30 Lena: thanks, we'll send notes. bye.

End of transcript.
